green.notes: Eighth remediation pass. 227/227 tests, tsc clean. New DELETE /v1/articles/{id}/images/{id} route (discardImage.ts) giving writers a way to discard a not-ready image row, running as service_role with no new PostgREST grant; migration 0005 adds a partial unique index enforcing one ready cover per article; render.ts falls back to the persisted structured_data.image when no live ready cover exists. verify.notes: IMPORTANT: this gate's own verdict, on its own criteria, was NOT PASSED — 05-verification.v8.md §11 states this explicitly. Status is recorded here as "passed" only because of the product-owner override logged below (overrides[0]), not because the gate's acceptance criteria were met. Read 05-verification.v8.md in full before treating this branch as verified; do not infer from status=passed alone that every finding was closed. Eight verify passes were run against this branch (v1-v8, one per remediation cycle); the full chain is preserved in pdlc/arsene-cms/ and pdlc/arsene-cms/verify/ and indexed in the log below. Findings genuinely and fully closed by v8, confirmed by independent adversarial testing: the discard route's core mechanism (CAS race, grant boundary, draft-lock check), M-V7-02 (render cover-blanking), and the practical effect of L-V7-01 (cover uniqueness) on a freshly-migrated database. Findings NOT closed, and the subject of the override: (1) migration 0005 cannot apply to a database already holding duplicate ready-cover rows, a state proven reachable through ordinary concurrent use with no attacker — 05-verification.v8.md §4; (2) the discard route has no src/api/client.ts method and no contract declaration, so the product's own editor SPA cannot currently call the route this whole cycle exists to provide — 05-verification.v8.md §5. Also open, not blocking: L-V8-01 (discard route has no rate limit or audit trail), L-V8-02 (discard permanently orphans the file in Supabase Storage), plus the standing backlog carried since v3-v7 (L-V7-02 updated_at forgeable, I-V7-01 missing CHECK constraint, L-V6-01 CDN_ORIGIN validation, L-V6-03 transient slug race, N5/N5b, N2, idempotency store TTL/writer_id scoping). Counter-metric (writer adoption) remains honestly uncomputable from any event this build emits, unchanged since the architecture gate; required events draft_started/article_published both confirmed emitted correctly via the real primary path across every one of the eight verify passes' instrumentation proofs, most recently §10 of 05-verification.v8.md.

pipeline.notes: IMPORTANT: status is "partial", not "passed" - this is a deliberate, distinct status, not an override. The architecture document (02-architecture.v1.md §6) named Supabase Edge Functions (Deno, Fetch-API handler model) as the API server's deploy target, but the code as built runs on Node's http.createServer and relies on node:child_process.spawn() - a different execution model that does not translate. This was invisible through eight remediation cycles because every test exercised the code via a real spawned Node child process, never asking whether that process could run on the platform the architecture named. Per this gate's own instructions, this is 'a finding to take back rather than a gap to improvise around' - raised with the product owner mid-gate; direction given was to build and rehearse the part that is real and document the rest as blocking. WHAT IS DONE AND REHEARSED FOR REAL: the Postgres migration deploy/rollback mechanism (scripts/deploy-migrations.sh, idempotent, tracked in a _migrations_applied table) was rehearsed three ways against a real local Postgres 16 container - fresh deploy (1.08s), no-op re-deploy (0.24s), incremental deploy (0.29s) - and the known migration-0005 one-way-door from verify v8 was reproduced for real (exact error, 0.09s to fail, no corruption) and its fix verified (0.09s to succeed after a tested pre-flight reconciliation step, not yet automated into the migration itself). All five migrations (0001-0005) confirmed expand-only by inspection. WHAT IS BLOCKED: the API server has no deploy or rollback mechanism - .github/workflows/deploy.yml's deploy-api-server job and rollback.yml's redeploy-api-server job are explicit, loudly-failing stubs naming this gap rather than silently omitting it. Two paths recorded in 10-pipeline.v1.md §2 for whoever makes this call: port the transport layer to Deno's Fetch-API model, or deploy the Node server as-is to a Node-compatible host (which reopens ADR-0001's $0/mo cost rationale). Separately, no Cloudflare Pages deployable artifact exists anywhere in this codebase (no Next.js app, no build script) - that half of the architecture's rollback plan belongs to a codebase that doesn't exist yet, in this repo or elsewhere. Tag v0.1.0 created locally (matches CHANGELOG.md) but not pushed.

overrides.reason: After eight red/green/verify remediation cycles (2026-08-11 through 2026-08-20), verify v8 (05-verification.v8.md) found the underlying server-side security and correctness work fully sound under independent adversarial testing — the new discard route's safety argument, CAS race handling, and grant boundary all survived from-scratch adversarial re-derivation by two independent verify agents, and no High-severity finding exists anywhere in the current state. What remained open were two Medium findings about reach rather than correctness: (1) migration 0005's cover-uniqueness index cannot apply to a database already holding the duplicate-cover state a prior finding (L-V7-01) proved reachable through ordinary use; (2) the new recovery route has no client method or contract declaration, so the product's own editor SPA cannot call it yet. Product owner reviewed this specific finding set and decided to ship as-is, accepting both as known, tracked limitations rather than continuing remediation before shipping.

accepted_findings.summary: Migration 0005 (partial unique index on article_images enforcing one ready cover per article) aborts with a Postgres uniqueness-violation error if applied to a database that already holds duplicate ready-cover rows on one article — a state 05-verification.v7.md §6 (L-V7-01) proved reachable through ordinary concurrent cover uploads, no attacker required. No test in the suite can catch this because every test database starts empty (tests/support/pg.ts). Recommended fix (not yet applied): a pre-flight step in the migration demoting all but the most-recently-created ready cover on each article before creating the index, plus a red-gate test that migrates a database seeded with the duplicate state rather than only an empty one.
accepted_findings.risk_if_unaddressed: If this branch is ever deployed to a database that has already exhibited the L-V7-01 duplicate-cover state, the migration will fail loudly (blocking the deploy, requiring manual data surgery) under a stop-on-error runner, or may silently never create the index under a more tolerant one — in which case cover uniqueness is not actually enforced in that environment despite the code and tests suggesting it is.

accepted_findings.summary: The DELETE /v1/articles/{id}/images/{id} discard route (src/api/discardImage.ts), the writer-facing recovery mechanism this entire eighth remediation cycle exists to build, has no method on src/api/client.ts and is documented in contracts/openapi.yaml as prose only, not a declared path item. The server-side capability is complete, correct, and thoroughly verified (see verify §2); nothing in the current codebase lets the actual editor SPA construct a request to it.
accepted_findings.risk_if_unaddressed: A writer whose article becomes permanently stuck (per the two routes documented in 05-verification.v7.md §4) has no way to recover through the actual product UI until a client method and contract declaration are added — only a direct HTTP request (e.g. via curl or a future SPA release) can currently invoke the fix.

not_accepted_as_blocking_but_tracked: L-V8-01: the discard route has no rate limit and writes no telemetry/audit record (pdlc/arsene-cms/05-verification.v8.md §6)
L-V8-02: every discard permanently orphans its file in Supabase Storage, with no cleanup path anywhere in the codebase (pdlc/arsene-cms/05-verification.v8.md §6)
